title: Integral pullback and completed tensor product preserve constructibility
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer
$\varpi_E$, $A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$, and a morphism $f:X\to Y$ of
schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible. Let $D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ ($W\in\{X,Y\}$)
be the derived-complete integral constructible categories, and let $Lf^*$ and
$\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}$ be the integral derived pullback and
completed tensor product. Then:

1. for $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ one has $Lf^*K\in D^b_c(X,\mathcal O_E)$,
and for every $n$ the canonical map gives
$(Lf^*K)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\cong f^{-1}(K\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$;
2. for $M,N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$ one has
$M\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}N\in D^b_c(W,\mathcal O_E)$, and
$(M\widehat\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}N)\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n}\cong
(M\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})\otimes^L_{A_{E,n}}(N\otimes^L_{\mathcal O_E}A_{E,n})$
for every $n$.

proof.text: For a good integral complex, use the object/map formulas for ordinary reduction to compare its actual reduction with changeOfRingsComplex. Transport K-flatness through this isomorphism using the tensor bifunctor. Apply changeOfRings_isKFlat_of_flat_terms. Good representatives of all derived objects are supplied by the proved independent-coefficient K-flat resolution theorem and the site/monoidal tensor comparison.

Apply the separate Roos-effectivity lemma to the pullback and tensor towers on arbitrary good representatives. Transport along the defining natural comparisons of the integral operations. Expanding the hom of the representative isomorphism gives exactly integralPullbackFiniteComparison and integralTensorFiniteComparison, including the actual Roos projections. This proves completeness and invertibility for every representative before using constructibility.

For finite coefficients pull back a constructible stratification using Stratification.pullback. The composition comparison for constant-module inverse image and the pullback preservation of finite local constancy show that every new stratum has finite locally constant restriction. Transport this assertion along cohomology isomorphisms. The proved comparison integralFinitePullbackModel and exact inverse image identify the cohomology of the finite pullback with pullback of input cohomology. Additivity preserves zero, so the same interval works at every level.

Use integral_residue_tor on the residue cohomology interval of the first tensor input. Transfer this uniform Tor bound to its actual finite reduction by the K-flat representative comparison. Identify the explicit finite tensor with categorical derived tensor using its K-flat first factor. The generic source-library theorem homologyConcentratedIn_tensor_of_torAmplitudeIn_left adds its Tor interval to the cohomology interval of the second factor. Thus all finite tensors have one common finite support interval; a second Tor-amplitude test is unnecessary.

Apply finiteTensor_constructible_cohomology to the two actual reductions, resolving the K-flat first one by its identity. The uniform support interval makes the cohomological support finite. Transport finite constructibility along the canonical reduction isomorphisms, using closure under isomorphisms of the bounded constructible category. Combine this with completeness and the interval to verify every clause of sfIntegralConstructible, for pullback and tensor.
